title: The PT-USDe instance carries three separate rate limits because the same position has three exit routes with different counterparty risk
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.4.3.2.4 splits one instance's limits into three named sub-documents: "Deposit Rate Limits (via FalconX)" at 50 million USDC max and 50 million slope (A...4.3.2.4.1), "Withdrawal Rate Limits (via FalconX)" identically at 50 million (A...4.3.2.4.2), and "Redemption Rate Limits (via Pendle Protocol)" at `Unlimited` (A...4.3.2.4.3). The instance also records a "Broker Address" (A...4.3.2.2.3) alongside the token and underlying addresses.

Each of these moves the same asset, so the limits cannot be measuring the asset. They are measuring the **venue**. Both FalconX legs pass through an OTC broker: a bilateral, off-chain-settled relationship where the failure mode is counterparty non-performance and the correct control is a cap in both directions — which is why the withdrawal leg is capped here even though withdrawals are unlimited elsewhere.

Redemption through Pendle is unlimited because it is the trustless route. As established in the Pendle procedure (A...2.1.2.11.1.2), Grove only redeems **after market expiry**, when PT converts at the PY index with no market price and no discretionary counterparty. There is nothing to ration.

The generalisable principle: rate limits should be keyed to the trust assumption of the path, and a position with a trustless exit deserves an unconstrained one. It also implies a hierarchy for stress — the unlimited Pendle route is the exit of last resort, available only once the market has expired, which is a timing constraint no limit configuration can relax.
description: FalconX deposits and withdrawals are each capped at 50 million USDC while redemption through Pendle at expiry is unlimited — the limit prices the route, not the asset.
